step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows an ETL and data processing pipeline for Depop's product recommendation engine. 1. Incoming event streams are received by Amazon Kinesis. 2. An AWS Lambda function fans out events into topic-specific Kinesis streams. 3. The data is written to Amazon S3 as raw JSON. 4. AWS Glue ETL jobs process the raw data from S3 (marked '1') and write transformed Parquet data back to S3 (marked '1A'). 5. Amazon Athena queries the Parquet dataset in S3 for the recommendation engine (group '2'). 6. AWS Lambda orchestrates the execution flow between Athena queries and Amazon EMR. 7. Amazon EMR computes product rankings and recommendations.

edges.notes: Ingested events sent to fan-out Lambda

Glue writes normalized Parquet data back to S3 (labeled '1A')
Athena queries processed dataset stored in S3
Athena query results trigger recommendation workflow via Lambda
